transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have a proposed sale of our $12 million commercial receivables pool to Meridian Receivables Fund on the table. Their draft offer is $11.7 million with requests for customary seller support on collection shortfalls. Before I can authorize this transaction and set closing conditions, I need each of your areas to report any unresolved items from the pre-closing cross-functional review. Let's start with legal, then credit risk, servicing operations, and financial crime compliance. What are we looking at?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue before we go any further. I confirmed with buyer's counsel this morning that Meridian will actually pay exactly $11,400,000 — not the $11,700,000 in the draft proposal — and only for a non-recourse true sale. Critically, any seller guarantee of collection shortfalls would invalidate the agreed structure entirely. This email has not yet been attached to the transaction file, which is why it hasn't surfaced in our review materials. The draft proposal's $11.7 million figure and its request for seller support on collection shortfalls are fundamentally inconsistent with what Meridian's counsel has actually agreed to.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical credit risk issue. While reviewing the debtor tape this week, I found that the largest obligor represents 18% of the pool — well above our bank's 10% single-obligor threshold. Credit policy therefore requires a $1,200,000 first-loss reserve before we can close this transaction. My revised concentration worksheet documenting this is not yet in the risk system, which is why it hasn't surfaced in the review materials so far. This concentration issue needs to be resolved before Elena authorizes the sale.

I confirmed with the lockbox bank this morning that collections can be redirected on June 15, 2026, but only if the transaction includes a lockbox activation commitment effective on that date. This confirmation is still in my operations email and has not been circulated to the rest of the team or attached to the transaction file, which is why it hasn't surfaced in our review materials. Any closing schedule or authorization decision needs to account for this lockbox activation requirement.

Upload the revised concentration worksheet to the risk system documenting the 18% single-obligor concentration and the required $1.2M first-loss reserve.
